title: How do parallel sides give all four angles?
description: A four sided figure has two pairs of parallel sides and a line from one corner to the opposite corner. Interior angles on the same side add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, and a split angle is added back together. Keeko doubts the answer, because Keeko thinks one angle is the same as its neighbour.
teaching_notes: One idea: with parallel sides, interior angles on the same side add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, so each neighbouring angle of the figure comes from the one before. Watch for students who copy one angle onto its neighbour.

source: A four-sided figure ABCD has AB parallel to CD and AD parall
video_script.why: The child uses interior angles on the same side, and the addition of a split angle, to find every angle of a four sided figure with parallel sides.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure: four sided figure ABCD with AB parallel to CD, AD parallel to BC and a line from A to C, angle DAC is sixty five degrees and angle ADC is sixty degrees
video_script.anchor: a four sided figure ABCD with AB parallel to CD, AD parallel to BC, a line from A to C inside it, angle DAC marked 65° and angle ADC marked 60°
video_script.wrong_answer: angle D eigh B is sixty
video_script.wrong_move: copies the size of angle ADC onto angle DAB, instead of using the sum of 180 for interior angles
video_script.payoff_line: Neighbouring angles of this figure add up to one hundred and eighty

final_answer.value: Angle DAB = 120°, angle CAB = 55°, angle BCD = 120°, angle ABC = 60°
final_answer.spoken: angle D eigh B is one hundred and twenty degrees, angle C eigh B is fifty five degrees, angle B C D is one hundred and twenty degrees, and angle eigh B C is sixty degrees

hold_back: Angle DAB = 120°, angle CAB = 55°, angle BCD = 120°, angle ABC = 60°
maths_rules: AB is parallel to CD and AD is a transversal, so angle ADC + angle DAB = 180
angle DAB = angle DAC + angle CAB, so 120 = 65 + angle CAB and angle CAB = 120 - 65 = 55
AD is parallel to BC and CD is a transversal, so angle ADC + angle BCD = 180 and angle BCD = 180 - 60 = 120
AD is parallel to BC and AB is a transversal, so angle DAB + angle ABC = 180 and angle ABC = 180 - 120 = 60
video_script.design: One figure for the whole video. Each pair of interior angles is filled in one colour when it is used, and the split angle at the corner A shows its two smaller angles.

<bookmark mark='diag'/>A line joins eigh and C.
<bookmark mark='given'/>The angle D eigh C is sixty five degrees. The angle eigh D C is sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the angles D eigh B, C eigh B, B C D and eigh B C.

<bookmark mark='split'/>A line from a corner splits an angle into two smaller angles that add up to the whole.
